name: surface-field
title: Surface Field
description: A themeable field of dots and lines that makes room around surfaces, bends as they move, and is lit by a light that follows the pointer.
author: Angelo Libero <https://github.com/angelolibero>
docs:
Installed `SurfaceField` in `components/ui/`, its drawing engine in `lib/` (`surface-field-engine`, `surface-field-dom`, `surface-field-controller`, `surface-field-viewport`) and the `render-loop` helper. Put it in a box that has a size and a background, behind your content: ```tsx import { SurfaceField } from "@/components/ui/surface-field";
Your content
``` The field draws no background, never intercepts the pointer and is `aria-hidden`. Its dots take the colour of `--surface-field-ink` (falling back to the inherited text colour) and the light blends toward `--surface-field-tint`; both have light and dark values in your theme, and a `tint` of 0 turns the blend off. To make room around your own objects, create a controller once (`createSurfaceFieldController()`, kept in `useMemo`), pass it as `controller` and send rectangles with `controller.setScene({ root, rects })`, in CSS pixels relative to `root`; moving objects go through `setFootprint` without a React render. Scene coordinates are physical pixels and do not flip in right-to-left pages. Use `refreshTheme()` after changing the colour on an ancestor other than the document root. Drawing pauses off screen and in hidden tabs (the `render-loop` helper); under reduced motion the field is drawn once, with no light, drift or breath. Ported from angelolibero/surface-field (MIT, copyright 2026 Angelo Libero); the license text is in every file. Its `worker` prop is not ported: the field always draws on the main thread, through the render loop.
